knowledge:
- key_parameters: multicore=FALSE ;; Controls whether qualSample parallelizes the calculation of sample SNRs using the parallel package.
- alternatives: impute package ;; Mentioned as a tool to impute missing values (NAs) in the gene expression matrix before calculating sample SNRs, since qualSample does not accept NAs.
- when_to_use: Appropriate for assessing the quality of gene expression studies (especially microarrays) and identifying problematic samples, particularly in studies containing a large number of diverse samples (e.g., cancer tissues).
- pitfalls: Input data must have probes mapped to gene IDs. qualSample cannot handle missing values (NAs), so they must be imputed or removed beforehand. A low study SNR does not always indicate poor experimental quality; it can also result from low biological variability (e.g., comparing cell lines in highly controlled conditions). Sample SNRs are relative to their study, meaning a very poor study might not show any outlier samples, and a flagged sample in a high-quality study might still be of acceptable absolute quality.

workflows.name: study_quality_assessment
workflows.intent: Estimate the overall signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of a gene expression study to assess its quality.
input: ALL (an ExpressionSet or gene expression matrix mapped to gene IDs)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the SNAGEE package and the dataset. 2. Calculate the study-level quality score using qualStudy. 3. Print the resulting SNR score.
workflows.code:
library(SNAGEE)
library(ALL)
data(ALL)
q = qualStudy(ALL)
print(q)

workflows.name: sample_quality_assessment
workflows.intent: Determine the relative signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs) of individual samples within a study to flag potentially problematic samples.
input: ALL (an ExpressionSet or gene expression matrix with no missing values, mapped to gene IDs)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the SNAGEE package and the dataset. 2. Calculate individual sample quality scores using qualSample. 3. Identify samples with quality scores below the threshold of -5.
workflows.code:
library(SNAGEE)
library(ALL)
data(ALL)
qs = qualSample(ALL, multicore=FALSE)
sum(qs < -5)
